text:
Cole Sillinger grew up in Columbus and plays for the Blue Jackets, and this season he's turning into a dependable middle-six forward. He has four goals and eight points in 15 games, with his best night a goal and an assist in the 7-2 rout of Colorado on Nov 3.

His finishing is honest: four goals on 3.7 expected (the quality of his chances). The worry is the chance share. Columbus has 47% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, slightly worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey noted that last season his results ran ahead of his chances while he played with strong teammates.

He's 23, the 12th pick in 2021, and already past 380 NHL games, which is easy to forget. He scored only eight goals last season, so even a modest pace is progress. Our projection sees about 17 goals. To get there with a better line, he'll need the Blue Jackets to stop getting outchanced when he's out.
